title: Tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) overdose
population: Adults and children (one pathway; ADULT / CHILD lines where doses differ)
dagger_note: † = clinical or local addition, not in the SA guideline
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold, k=kind (check|value|yn|info|sub), h=heading

admission.title: Diagnostic criteria — TCA ingestion + any feature below (clinical)

items.t: Known or suspected TCA ingestion (e.g. amitriptyline)
Anticholinergic: sedation, delirium, tachycardia, dilated pupils, urinary retention, dry mouth
Cardiovascular: QRS widening, ventricular dysrhythmias, hypotension
Neurological: altered mental status, coma, seizures
May be well on arrival and deteriorate rapidly. Serious toxicity may occur with low doses in children.

decision.t: 10. Diagnosis = SEVERE TCA poisoning → alkalinise, then REFER (ICU). Adult: ICU if ventilatory or circulatory support needed; child: any arrhythmia → refer
11. ADMIT — continuous ECG monitoring — stabilise, then continue on the 0 h – discharge inpatient chart and the 24-hour nursing record

chart.phase_note: Alkalinise whenever the criteria are met, not on the clock

standing.t: Cardiac monitor continuously; child: cardiac and ECG monitoring for 48 h
12-lead ECG on arrival, after every bicarbonate bolus, then 6-hourly until normal for 24 h
Hourly for the first 24 h and while QRS > 100 ms or on bicarbonate, then 4-hourly: HR, BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature, GCS, pupils, monitor rhythm, bladder / urine
VBG (pH, K, Na) after every bicarbonate bolus and 4-hourly while alkalinising
HGT on arrival and with any seizure or drop in LOC

rows.label: 0 h
rows.lead: Check the referral note for charcoal, benzodiazepines and fluids already given. Call Poisons Helpline 0861 555 777 or UFS 082 491 0160 (24 h).

feed.t: Airway, O₂, IV access, cardiac monitor
Symptomatic: be prepared to intubate early → REFER (ventilation)
Activated charcoal once airway protected — works for longer than usual (TCAs delay gastric emptying); doses in Doses tab
Gastric lavage seldom: experienced staff, airway protected; adult ≤ 60 min; child: large ingestion or within a few hours
Hypotension — child: NaCl 0.9% or Ringer's lactate 20 mL/kg IV bolus
Hypotension — adult: crystalloid in titrated boluses up to 1 L

tests.t: 12-lead ECG — all patients: QRS ____ ms, rhythm
If intentional or unknown: paracetamol level (≥ 4 h)
If female of child-bearing age: urine βhCG
Record time of ingestion on request forms

treatment.h: Alkalinise if ventricular dysrhythmia · QRS > 100 ms · hypotension unresponsive to fluids · seizures

treatment.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% IV, 1–2 mL/kg as bolus doses (child: 1–2 mEq/kg) — target pH 7.45–7.55
Monitor acid-base, K and Na. Specialist / Poisons Centre consultation
Bicarbonate unavailable or fluid-restricted: hyperventilate if intubated (adult)
ADULT: lorazepam 4 mg IV, or midazolam 10 mg IV (IM/buccal if no IV), or diazepam 10 mg IV; repeat once at 5 min
ADULT: no phenytoin (toxin, cardiotoxic) — still seizing: REFER
CHILD: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg), or midazolam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg) / 0.5 mg/kg buccal, or diazepam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg); repeat once at 5 min
CHILD: then phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV over 5 min (max 600 mg). No phenytoin. REFER
No flumazenil in mixed overdose (convulsions, dysrhythmias)
Severe: inotropes / anti-arrhythmics needed → REFER (ICU)
Child: any arrhythmia → REFER

tests.t: VBG (pH, K, Na) after every bolus
12-lead ECG after every bolus — QRS ____ ms

treatment.t: Correct low K
Discuss with specialist / Poisons Centre
QRS still > 100 ms or dysrhythmia despite bicarbonate: REFER (ICU)

feed.t: Charcoal given? ____ g at ____. Fluid balance.

treatment.t: Bladder: catheter if retention
Restless: benzodiazepine (Doses tab)

feed.t: Maintenance fluids; nil by mouth while drowsy

treatment.t: Reassess severity (Arrival §2): any criterion → alkalinise, consider REFER
Lung bases — crepitations = overload / pulmonary oedema
Intentional: start mental health assessment when alert
Still drowsy, broad QRS or hypotensive: REFER (ICU)

feed.t: Bicarbonate stopped if QRS normal and stable. Oral diet

tests.t: 12-lead ECG — normal for 24 h? Y / N
VBG if bicarbonate given in last 24 h

treatment.t: Adult: asymptomatic, or mild and ECG normal ≥ 24 h → medically fit
Intentional: mental health assessment; refer to social, psychological or psychiatric services
Child: social worker if supervision or neglect concern
Child: 48 h cardiac and ECG monitoring complete → medically fit
Discharge criteria
Medicines reviewed: TCA stopped or small supply
Safety counselling

items.t: Ventricular dysrhythmia · QRS > 100 ms · hypotension unresponsive to fluids · seizures
1–2 mL/kg bolus doses (child: 1–2 mEq/kg) to pH 7.45–7.55
Adult: crystalloid in titrated boluses up to 1 L; avoid overload
Child: NaCl 0.9% or Ringer's lactate 20 mL/kg IV bolus

items.h: Activated charcoal — airway protected; effective for longer than usual in TCA overdose

items.t: Child < 6 y: 1 g/kg in 50–100 mL water
Child > 6 y: 20–50 g in 100–300 mL water

items.h: Seizures / restlessness — benzodiazepine, repeat once at 5 min; never phenytoin

items.t: Adult: lorazepam 4 mg IV · or midazolam 10 mg IV (IM/buccal if no IV) · or diazepam 10 mg IV. Not controlled: REFER (refractory)
Child (< 13 y): lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4) · or midazolam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10) / 0.5 mg/kg buccal · or diazepam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10)
Child: then phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 600 mg). REFER
QRS still > 100 ms or dysrhythmia despite bicarbonate
New crepitations, rising RR or SpO₂ falling from baseline: stop boluses

discharge.title: Discharge criteria — all must be met (conditional items where they apply)

items.t: Adult: asymptomatic, or mild symptoms and ECG normal for ≥ 24 h
Child: 48 h cardiac and ECG monitoring completed
Intentional: mental health assessment and referral done
Child: safe storage counselling; social worker if concern

items.t: Mental health follow-up as referred (social, psychological or psychiatric services)
Return immediately if palpitations, fainting, seizure or confusion
